messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated inference tail latency detected in hosted API (region: us-west-2). P95 generation latency up from ~300ms to ~4.5s over the last 10m; connection backlog rising, streaming connections are piling up. Auto-scaling not keeping up. (metric snapshot: cpu_gpu_util=92%, active_streams=8.2k). Paging on-call.

alex_t: got the page, looking. Saw a couple of big spikes coinciding with several high-rate tenants. Repro: streaming responses are the main queueing pressure.

alex_t: paging @priya_r and @mike_sre — can you join? I'm going to triage and propose quick mitigations (rate caps, reduce streaming load, fallback to non-streaming).

priya_r: on it. Initial idea: prefer rate-limiting and per-tenant quota throttles before killing streaming entirely. Streaming is high-bandwidth but we can also drop concurrent stream limit per API key.

mike_sre: joining. If runtime can't reclaim KV cache fast enough, streams block GPUs. I can push conservative global rate cap at the edge and drop streaming concurrency for heavy tenants. If that doesn't stabilize, we'll toggle streaming off for hosted for 15m and route to normal generation.

priya_r: quick health checks:
```
# sample queries
curl -s https://metrics.redwood.ai/api/metrics?window=5m | jq '.latency.p95'
# -> 4.5s
```
Suggest patching streaming thread pool size + prefetched-kv limit, but those can take time to rollout. For immediate relief we have two fast actions: 1) set global streaming concurrency cap to 6000 connections, 2) apply per-tenant burst token bucket to top-10 tenants.

mike_sre: applying edge rate limit now via admin API. running:
```
POST https://admin-infra.redwood/v1/ratelimits
{ "scope": "hosted:streaming", "limit": 6000 }
```
(ops-bot: deploy-guard: started rate-limit update)

ops-bot: CONFIG UPDATE: rate-limit scope=hosted:streaming limit=6000 accepted; propagated to 4 edge clusters.

mike_sre: initial drop lowered active_streams to ~5.6k but latency P95 only fell to ~2.1s. Still above SLO. Next step: per-tenant token quota for top offenders — applying temporary 50% throttle for tenants: tenant-A, tenant-B, tenant-C.

jordan_support: listing customers seeing degraded streaming: tenant-A (high), tenant-B (medium), tenant-D (bursting occasional). I can reach out with an interim note if we plan to disable streaming for all hosted customers.

priya_r: thanks. Two quick safety toggles if throttles don't finish: a) set flag streaming.enabled=false for hosted runtime, or b) add a header transform at the edge to force non-streaming responses. I prefer header transform so customers still get full responses, just not chunked. Example curl to flip flag in feature store:
```
PATCH https://config.redwood/v1/features/streaming
{ "scope": "hosted", "enabled": false }
```

This is risky but fast. Can be rolled back immediately.

lucy_product: if we disable streaming we'll need a short customer message explaining we're temporarily reverting to non-streaming to stabilize latency and throughput; ETA 15-30m. Jordan, can you draft a templated note? Keep it clear: degraded functionality (no streaming), same outputs, faster recovery.

jordan_support: drafting now. Proposed text: "We're temporarily disabling streaming responses for hosted API to stabilise latency. Responses will arrive as a single payload rather than streamed chunks. No data loss. Expect restored streaming within ~30m. Reach out if you see errors."

alex_t: decision checkpoint: throttles in place but P95 still high. We have customer impact (support list). I approve temporary non-streaming fallback for hosted for up to 30m while we monitor. Priya, Mike — please execute header transform to disable streaming at the edge ASAP.

priya_r: executing header transform patch:
```
POST https://edge-admin.redwood/v1/transforms
{ "name": "force-non-streaming", "condition": "route==/v1/generate && deployment==hosted", "actions": [{"set_header": {"x-redwood-force-non-stream": "true"}}] }
```
(ops-bot: deploy-transform: started)

ops-bot: TRANSFORM APPLY: force-non-streaming applied to us-west-2 and us-east-1 edges.

mike_sre: monitoring... within 90s P95 dropped to ~420ms, active_streams decayed to ~800. GPU queue depth normalized. Good signal.

lucy_product: thanks team. Jordan, go ahead and send the interim notification to affected customers with that wording. Mark as "investigating" and reference our incident link.

jordan_support: sent messages to tenant-A and tenant-B. Both acknowledged; tenant-A said they can tolerate the fallback.

alex_t: on-call handoff note — I'll be on the next 20min to finish ramp-down and then hand to @priya_r for the next shift. Priya, please keep this open as a follow-up and run canary re-enable when stable.

priya_r: will do. Immediate next steps for post-mitigation: 1) capture samples from top offenders to understand why streaming connections were long-lived, 2) add smarter KV eviction in runtime, 3) implement gradual streaming warmup for large responses.

mike_sre: also action: add alert rule for streaming connection growth > 3k/min and automated soft throttle at 5k. Filing ticket SRE-1123.

ops-bot: NOTE: transform force-non-streaming will expire in 30m unless extended.

priya_r: adding config to canary re-enable: will flip header transform off in a single edge and watch metrics for 10m. If stable, roll to others.

alex_t: thanks all. Current status: mitigation applied (streaming -> non-streaming fallback via header transform), edge rate limits + per-tenant throttles active. Latency and GPU queueing returned to normal. Support notified. Keeping thread open for re-enable canary and postmortem tasks. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: RESOLVED? Noting manual intervention — transform applied; incident severity downgraded to SEV-3.

priya_r: follow-up: will schedule postmortem runbook and include timeline, root-cause hypotheses (KV eviction/backpressure), and action owners. Expected doc in 48h.

mike_sre: handing on-call to @priya_r now. I'll remain available if re-enable triggers trouble.

alex_t: handing off too, logging final notes and link to the support messages. Closing my loop.

jordan_support: monitoring replies from customers. Will escalate if any errors crop up.

priya_r: starting canary re-enable in 10m on a single low-traffic edge; will post updates here.

(10m later)
priya_r: canary re-enable done on canary-edge-1; no spike in p95 for 12m so far. Rolling to other edges slowly.

ops-bot: TRANSFORM REMOVE: force-non-streaming removed from us-west-2.

priya_r: full rollback of transform completed; streaming restored across hosted. Observed P95 stable at ~320ms, active_streams back at ~1.1k. Closing mitigation.

alex_t: great work. Recording final actions in incident tracker and scheduling postmortem.

mike_sre: filing SRE-1123 and assigning owners.

lucy_product: create a short status update for customers summarizing cause and mitigation. I'll own that.

incident-bot: THREAD CLOSED: incident automated tag=resolved; retention note added.
